series.note: The upset the brief asks about: the market had Aurora around 73-76% before lock (Pinnacle 9z 27% on our day-1 review; Polymarket priced Aurora 76c), only about 5% of Hotspawn players picked 9z, and 9z won 2-0 with a 13-1 Nuke.
NIP arrived as the replacement for Virtus.pro (announced 9 Oct) and pushed Falcons to overtime on Ancient before losing Dust II.
Ninjas in Pyjamas eliminated (0-2). Aurora's answer to the day-1 loss: they out-fragged NIP on both maps (Hotspawn day-2 review names Wicadia as the stand-out and notes stavn's 0.34 rating).
Falcons qualified for the playoffs (2-0). 9z lost their own Nuke pick 9-13, won Mirage 13-8 and lost the Dust II decider 9-13 - a three-map match against the event favourites.
PARIVISION eliminated (0-2). BetBoom reverse-swept after losing the opener.
FURIA qualified for the playoffs (2-0). Legacy took the opener on Cache then lost Inferno 5-13 and the Mirage decider 8-13.

situations.what: Summer rebuild that the brief asks about: coach Fabre benched 2026-06-29; MAJ3R and soulfly out 2026-07-02; Jimpphat (from MOUZ) and coach ashhh signed 2026-07-03; kyxsan acquired from Falcons as in-game leader 2026-07-08. The retained core is XANTARES, woxic and Wicadia, so the roster changed from a Turkish-language project to an international one around a new IGL.
situations.turnaround: 3.3 months before this decider (104 days for Jimpphat, 99 for kyxsan at the time the board read HLTV), so it is NOT a fresh change; it is the youngest of the playoff teams' systems, and coach ash said in August that the new system was still bedding in.
situations.verdict: Moderate factor against Aurora when she is a heavy favourite (this is why the board carries 9z as the SITUATIONAL play); it does not point the other way, and Aurora's day-2 2-0 shows the ceiling of the new five.

lessons: Day 1: all four favourites won except the one the market liked at about 73-76% - 9z 2-0 Aurora. The crowd had 5% on 9z; the outside market had 27-35%.

Day 2: the two favourites that had already won did it again (Falcons, FURIA), and both losers of day 1 who stayed alive did so by 2-0 over the teams that had lost too (Aurora, BetBoom). The gap between the top and bottom of each group was bigger than the gap the day-1 upset suggested.

Reading for day 3: the deciders are the only two matches left, both 1-1 vs 1-1, and both carry 7 points. Take the favourite (market side) for the headline pick, and keep the faded underdog as the leaderboard play where an outside price puts it above its crowd share - that is exactly the 9z case (31.5-34.8% priced vs 11% of players).

Contrarian but not stupid means: never fade a favourite just because the crowd is on it; fade only when at least two outside estimates, or one outside estimate plus our own line, put the underdog within reach and the crowd is far below that number.
